sentences.text: Caudipteryx is a genus of two known species of feathered theropod dinosaurs with an appearance so bird-like that some scientists initially thought it was a bird.
This small theropod measured between 72.5 and 89 cm in length, with some specimens reaching up to one meter, while weighing about 5 kg or between 6 and 7 kilograms.
Symmetrical, vane-bearing feathers with barbs and rachises measuring between 15 and 20 cm in length were held in its hands.
The animal possessed a bird-like beak covered with long upper teeth.
Its body was covered in silky, padded feathers, likely used to protect against the cold.
Long feathers may have been brightly colored solely to be displayed to scare enemies or attract mates.
Gastroliths have been preserved in at least two Caudipteryx specimens, NGMC 97 4 A and NGMC 97 9 A.
The presence of these stomach stones suggests the animal swallowed them to aid digestion.
Fossils of Caudipteryx were recovered in 1997 from the Sihetun locality in Liaoning province, China.
The type species Caudipteryx zoui was described in 1998, and Caudipteryx dongi was described in 2000.
The genus was named and identified by Philip Currie, Ji Qiang, Mark Norell, and Ji Shuan based on the holotype NGMC 97-4-A, a skeleton with feathers, and the paratype NGMC 97-9-A.

Studies of its flight feather count suggest that Caudipteryx was secondarily flightless, as the shortness and symmetry of the feathers, along with the short arms relative to body size, indicate that it could not fly.
Caudipteryx was a runner and likely very fast, although its speed has not been formally calculated, and researchers propose that it used its speed to escape large predators rather than to catch prey.
Caudipteryx is considered an omnivore that primarily fed on insects, small mammals, primitive birds, and lizards.
All known fossils of Caudipteryx come from the Yixian Formation in Liaoning, China.

The consensus classification places Caudipteryx as a basal member of the Oviraptorosauria, a group of non-avian theropod dinosaurs, and most paleontologists who performed cladistic analysis agree that it is a basal member of the family Oviraptoridae.
Lamanna et al. performed a cladistic analysis during the description of Anzu wyliei, placing Caudipteryx within Oviraptorosauria.
Caudipteryx lived in China during the Early Cretaceous, approximately 124.6 million years ago, in what is now Asia.
It lived during the Barremian to Aptian stages, from 125.77 to 119.57 million years ago.

It is debated whether Caudipteryx is a member of Oviraptorosauria, a bird, or both, and whether birds are or are not dinosaurs. Some researchers argue that Caudipteryx belongs within the bird lineage (Aves) rather than being a non-avian dinosaur. Not all scientists support the theory that Caudipteryx is indisputably non-avian; some, like Alan Feduccia, doubt the consensus that birds are theropods and argue Caudipteryx is a non-flying bird unrelated to dinosaurs. Halszka Osmolska et al. (2004) concluded in their cladistic analysis that Caudipteryx possesses more bird-like characteristics than current oviraptorids, placing the clade between birds and considering Caudipteryx to be both an oviraptorid and a bird.
